solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Typical Korean food Spooner orders (something other than dog)

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words here trade places

blocks.note: anything that is not a poodle is something other than a dog; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A cheeky jibe that Spooner, ordering Korean food, asks for anything but dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the N and P of NOT POODLE gives POT NOODLE, a British instant-noodle snack sold in a plastic pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant noodles in a pot are close kin to Korean ramyeon, a staple quick meal in Korea.

clue.text: Heathen dad runs away from his mum

indicators.note: running away from something means leaving it, so that letter departs from the word it was in

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A godless father abandons his own mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His mum' is read from the dad's side: his mother is the child's GRAN, which loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan follows no mainstream religion, which is what a heathen is: a synonym.

clue.text: Floating asset looking to return healthy net yield

definitions.text: Floating asset looking to return healthy net yield

blocks.clueFragment: Floating asset looking to return healthy net yield
blocks.note: surface reading: a share issue or investment hoping for a good profit after costs
setter's reading: a boat that floats, hoping to come back to port with plenty of fish in its net

explanation.walkthrough: 'Floating', 'asset' and 'net yield' all sound like finance; read literally they describe a fishing boat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing vessel floats, earns money for its owner, and hauls catches in a net, so all of it describes the boat.

clue.text: Ruling over road funding cancelled at the outset

indicators.note: cancelling the outset removes the very first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A decision about a road whose money was withdrawn before work started.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official decree, and a ruling is likewise an authoritative decision: synonyms.

clue.text: Delay the lav breaks where it's often too hot

indicators.note: something that breaks is smashed into pieces that can be put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting off loo breaks is a bad idea somewhere sweltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lav' is British slang for a lavatory, a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Death Valley in California is among the hottest places on Earth, a fitting example of a scorching location.

clue.text: English newspaper that's tanked domestically

blocks.note: the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: A British newspaper that has flopped on the home market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanked' suggests failure, but here it means kept in a tank at home, as a pet newt might be.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, an amphibian that people sometimes keep as a pet in an aquarium.

clue.text: One tending to animals taps fodder crop

blocks.note: the two taps on a basin are marked C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: A vet pats or sounds out an animal's feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant grown to feed livestock, a classic example of a forage crop.

clue.text: Noted Italian scuba enthusiast cycling

indicators.note: cycling goes round in a loop, so letters from the front of the word move round to the back

blocks.note: someone who loves scuba goes diving

explanation.surface: A famous Italian who loves diving also rides bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means famous on the surface, but hints at musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian composer of operas, a man known for writing notes.

clue.text: Still time for an idea

blocks.note: still in the sense of nevertheless
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: There is still time to come up with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective meaning motionless; it is the adverb 'however'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought is a notion formed in the mind, which is what an idea is: synonyms.

clue.text: Relating to heresy originally rooted in evil spell

indicators.note: done originally means made in a new, inventive way, so these letters are arranged afresh
one thing set in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

explanation.surface: Heresy is said to grow from a wicked curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heresy originally' tempts a solver to take H as a first letter; 'originally' goes with 'rooted' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodox beliefs depart from accepted doctrine, which is what heresy involves.

clue.text: King George VI & Mary of Teck (an older lady)

blocks.note: Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George
the ampersand read as a word
Queen Mary of Teck was George VI's mother, his ma

explanation.surface: A royal couple listing, with a parenthetical aside about an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary of Teck was wife of George V and mother of George VI, so to him she was Ma.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is typically an elderly woman of the family, so 'an older lady' describes her.

clue.text: Eject solicitor importing fake fur

indicators.note: something fake is made up, so these letters are made up into a new order
importing brings goods inside, so one piece is carried into the middle of another

blocks.note: a tout solicits custom, e.g. for tickets

explanation.surface: A lawyer smuggling counterfeit fur is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but it is one who solicits trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To turf out is an informal phrasal verb for forcing someone to leave, i.e. to throw them out.

clue.text: Material revenue-generating route for BA?

blocks.note: BA is British Airways, whose lucrative flagship route runs New York to London; NY is New York
LON is the abbreviation for London, the other end of that route

explanation.surface: Something substantial about a profitable British Airways route.
explanation.walkthrough: The NY-LON route between New York and London is one of the busiest and most profitable in aviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre made into cloth, so it is a fabric or material.

clue.text: Difficult letting go Democrat, periodically heavy drinker — Herald

indicators.note: letting something go means releasing it, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
someone who drinks heavily in bouts, on binges

explanation.surface: A hard-drinking newspaper man fires a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' looks like an alternate-letters signal but belongs to the description of the binge drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger announces something coming, as a herald proclaims news: synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Hamlet's friend rebelled — northern commander evacuated soldiers, we're told

indicators.note: something evacuated has been emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay
being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
first and last letters of the word
soldier ants; Antz is also the animated film about them

explanation.surface: Hamlet's friend revolted when a northern commander pulled his troops out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosencrantz is Hamlet's old school friend in Shakespeare's play, sent to spy on him.

clue.text: For each salesman getting a kickback

indicators.note: a kickback goes back the other way, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Every salesman receives a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Per is the Latin-derived preposition meaning for every one, as in a price per head.

clue.text: Secretary, single, receiving after tax sweetener at Xmas

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: income left after tax is net, also spelt nett

explanation.surface: An unmarried secretary is given a Christmas bonus after tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests a bribe or bonus; here it is a sweet thing eaten at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Panettone is an Italian sweet bread loaf traditionally eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Myopic northern listener quoted on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is taken by how it sounds

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A short-sighted listener from the north is quoted on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the condition of seeing near objects clearly but far ones poorly, i.e. being short-sighted.

clue.text: Throwing a strop, UB40 besieges posh boozer

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding on all sides, so the words before enclose the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, ignoring spaces and punctuation

explanation.surface: The reggae band UB40 lose their temper and surround an upmarket pub.
explanation.walkthrough: UB40 is a British reggae band; a 'boozer' is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub serving restaurant-quality food, an upmarket kind of drinking place.

clue.text: Country beginning to need NHS-related reforms

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
reforming something reshapes it, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A nation starting to need overhauls to its health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a European nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Inner London lawyer, part-timer, left bar having stolen book

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A temporary legal worker in London quit the bar after pinching a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner London' refers to the Inner Temple, one of the Inns of Court where barristers train.
explanation.definitionFit: A Templar is a lawyer or student with chambers in the Temple, the London legal district.

clue.text: Photographs put on page 9

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Pictures placed on page nine of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pix is informal shorthand for pictures, i.e. photos.

clue.text: One accustomed to cold open Guinness bottles?

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the words that follow hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone used to cold drinks opens bottles of Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Guinness adverts famously featured a penguin, which ties the surface to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguins live in Antarctic and other icy waters, so they are well used to freezing conditions.

clue.text: My two are excited about the introduction of Shania Twain's character

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter of the name is used
excited things are stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
about means around, so these letters wrap the other piece

explanation.surface: A parent's two children get excited about meeting the singer Shania Twain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shania' sets up singer Shania Twain, but the definition needs Mark Twain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.

clue.text: Tummy muscle floppy, fat behind

indicators.note: something floppy has no fixed shape, so these letters can be bent into another form

explanation.surface: A slack stomach and a fat backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical word meaning towards or at the stern, i.e. at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Peeled citrus fruit spread

indicators.note: peeling strips away the skin, so the outermost letters at both ends come off

blocks.note: citrus fruit taken as a plural

explanation.surface: Skinned citrus spread on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is the extent across which something varies, as a spread is: synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Nevertheless, with depleted oxygen the odds are 50-50

indicators.note: a depleted stock has been used up, so that letter is gone

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Even with low oxygen, the chances are equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens is the betting term for odds of one to one.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, evens means a stake wins the same amount back, an even chance either way.

clue.text: Light crude fuels?

blocks.note: surface reading: low-density unrefined oil used as fuel
setter's reading: a lamp, and crude oil fuels this lamp

explanation.walkthrough: 'Light crude' is an oil-industry grade; read as noun and verb, it says a light that crude oil fuels.
explanation.definitionFit: This lamp burns paraffin or other oil as fuel to give light.

clue.text: Drink up mate!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A cheery toast: drink up, friend!
explanation.definitionFit: Pal and mate are both informal British words for a friend: synonyms.

clue.text: Planet starts to notice extremely polluted air

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, which alone are kept from the next three

explanation.surface: A planet whose atmosphere is noticeably very dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' means atmosphere on the surface, but here it is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun in our solar system.

clue.text: Rue not starting winger

indicators.note: not starting means the word lacks its beginning, so its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to rue is to be sorry about

explanation.surface: Regretting that a wide player was left out of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football wide player; it is something with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a bird, and so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Sleazy, drunken retired nob, boring sluggard

indicators.note: a drunken walk lurches about, so the letters stagger into a new order
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the word runs the opposite way
boring means drilling into something, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A seedy, tipsy, retired aristocrat, dull and idle.
explanation.walkthrough: A nob is British slang for a wealthy or upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is an idle person, which is what a sluggard is: synonyms.
